demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: Pause, refuse, approve and resume on your machine
demos.purpose: The cell builds the kit's approval graph on a scripted model that asks for withdraw_document, with an in-memory checkpointer and an executor that only prints. It streams the turn to its pause and lists what waits. Then it tries Asha's own approval, and Ravi's. The pause is data in the checkpointer, not a request waiting in memory. The first process pauses the turn into a SQLite file, ~/lesson108_threads.db, through SqliteSaver, the local lane's checkpointer, and ends. The second process is a new interpreter: it builds a new graph on the same file, finds the waiting call, and resumes it with Ravi's approval. The same graph, now with a scripted model that asks Asha which rule applies to her. The handbook's NP-03 gives a confirmed employee at grade E3 or above 60 days' notice, and its PB-02 gives 15 days during probation. Ravi tries to answer for her, Asha tries to approve, then Asha answers. A resumed node runs again from its first line. The kit writes its "approval asked" line below interrupt(), so it is written once, at the resume. The first cell defines twice108, which pauses one withdrawal, approves it, and counts that line at each point. The second cell moves the line above interrupt(), from line 364 to line 361, and runs twice108 again. Then it puts the kit's file back with git, so the setup section's git pull next time is not refused.

demos.heading: Escalate and clarify over REST, on your lane
demos.purpose: The cell sends the gate's own request for a person on one session, then one of its near misses, "How do I contact HR about payroll?", which gate() reads as a question about a process and lets through. Then it raises the case the first reply offered and sends it with a token. Last, it withdraws the case as the person who raised it. It keeps the case's id in ~/lesson108_case.txt for step 7. Three turns. The handbook answers "What is my notice period?" two ways: 60 days for a confirmed employee at grade E3 or above (NP-03), and 15 days during probation (PB-02). The second turn gives, on the same session, the fact the first lacked. The third sends the same reply in a new session.

demos.heading: The approval wired in: a withdrawal paused on your lane, decided over REST, run by you
demos.purpose: The whole flow runs on the kit's own chat service with a fake Firestore and a scripted model, at Rs 0: the switch off, then on; the pause and its record; the hold; the requester's own approval refused; another company's approver and a colleague without the role seeing nothing; the second person's approval; a rejection beside a search; a question only the asker answers; an expired record, and the hold ending its pause; a lost pause; and --approved on the record. 18 tests, in ~/graph-venv from step 4. make agent-actions writes agent_actions into acme's tenant_settings, beside the Desk's switches, and prints them; the chat service reads it within a minute. make roles gives documind-evalacme-sa the doc_approver role beside employee: the eval account stands in for a colleague who may approve, as it stood in for an acme employee in lesson 5.6. The requester will be documind-ui-sa, on acme's roster since lesson 5.1's smoke. make smoke-approval runs the flow once against your chat service, printing each step. As documind-ui-sa it asks the LangGraph brain to withdraw townhall_2026_q1.md, a small acme document: the turn pauses, and the reply carries the record. The same session's next question is held. The requester's own approval is refused. documind-evalzeta-sa, on zeta's roster, cannot tell the record exists. The approver's list shows it. documind-evalacme-sa approves it, and the turn resumes: the tool runs, records the approved withdrawal, and the model answers that the operator will run it. A second decision is refused. Then a second withdrawal on a new session, which the approver rejects with a reason: the call errors alone and the model says nothing was withdrawn. The smoke withdraws nothing; it ends by printing your next two commands. The approval queued the work; you run it. The cell reads the approved record's id as the requester, runs make withdraw-run for it, and lists acme's sources, where the document's ledger row now says withdrawn. Acme's approval records from Firestore, oldest first, and today's approval events in the audit bucket, read without the chat service. make restore lifts the tombstone, as lesson 1.7 showed, and the worker returns the document. Then make agent-actions writes off, and acme's LangGraph brain is again the one lessons 5.4, 5.5 and 5.7 show, within a minute.

A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. The pin back is a separate window on purpose: pasted together with the line above, it would put acme straight back on RAG Engine before the lesson began. Leave it until the lesson's last step is done.
